title: Metal lowering declares threadgroup memory the pipeline dead-code-eliminates for multi-SIMD-group elementwise kernels

evidence.note: run_fault harness_fault at environment stage, turn 1: 'Metal archive helper observations differ from the admitted pipeline'; 2,370,740 provider tokens burned
candidate lowering with 1024 lanes (32 SIMD groups), purely elementwise body; line 17 declares 'threadgroup float share[32]' which the body never references
compiled pipeline reports static_threadgroup_memory_bytes=0 (allocation eliminated) while the declared toolchain requirements said 128 bytes

observation: src/open_cake_ir/compiler/backends/metal.py:359-366 emits 'threadgroup float share[N]' unconditionally whenever SIMD groups > 1, and lab/metal_build.py:201 forces (>32 threads iff threadgroup memory declared). A purely elementwise multi-group kernel therefore declares 128 bytes it never uses; the Metal compiler eliminates the unused allocation, the sealed archive's pipeline observation reports 0, and the strict declared==observed check at lab/metal_build.py:68-71 raises a campaign-fatal harness_fault on a semantically harmless candidate.
proposed_change: Emit share[] only when the schedule actually lowers a cross-SIMD-group collective through threadgroup memory, and report threadgroup_memory_bytes from that same fact. Decouple the threads/tgmem XOR rule so a 1024-thread elementwise kernel may declare zero. Keep the declared==observed strictness in the validator unchanged - the declaration should become truthful, not the check looser.
verification_plan: Bug-fix tick, replay-verified: re-lower the exact candidate source retained in the silu-20260909c workspace under the successor Executor/Compiler revision; the same build must pass pipeline admission.
